purpose: Trigger a Devin session in Slack from any channel by tagging @Devin. Devin responds in-thread; users continue the conversation in the thread. Attachments supported.

flags.name: <message>
flags.doc: The task instructions. May include code snippets, URLs, attachments.

examples.invocation: @Devin please bump the lodash version in this repo and open a PR
examples.expected_output: Devin opens a thread, acknowledges, and starts working
examples.scenario: Trivial dependency bump initiated from Slack

purpose: Trigger a Devin session from a Microsoft Teams channel or chat. Devin responds in-thread.

examples.invocation: @Devin investigate why CI is failing on PR 1234
examples.expected_output: Devin acknowledges and posts a session link
examples.scenario: Bug-triage from Teams

purpose: Get a quick codebase answer without spinning up a full agent session. Available in Slack and Teams. Lower-cost alternative to a full session for read-only questions.

flags.name: <question>
flags.doc: Question text — typically a 'where is X?' / 'how does Y work?' type query.

examples.invocation: !ask where is the rate limiter implemented in our auth service?
examples.expected_output: Quick answer with file references — no agent session created
examples.scenario: Codebase navigation in Slack

purpose: Deeper research answer using advanced search. Higher-effort variant of !ask. Available in Slack and Teams.

flags.name: <question>
flags.doc: Question requiring multi-file search and reasoning.

examples.invocation: !deep what's the full request flow when a user uploads an avatar?
examples.expected_output: Multi-step traced answer with cross-file citations
examples.scenario: Architecture-level question in Slack

purpose: Prevent Devin from seeing further messages in the current thread. Useful when humans need to confer without Devin reacting.

examples.invocation: mute
examples.expected_output: Devin stops processing thread messages
examples.scenario: Side-conversation between human reviewers in Devin's run thread

purpose: Re-enable Devin's processing of thread messages after a `mute`.

examples.invocation: unmute
examples.expected_output: Devin resumes processing thread messages
examples.scenario: Re-engaging Devin after a side-conversation

purpose: Cause Devin to ignore a single message (useful for commenting on Devin's run directly in-thread without affecting Devin's behavior).

examples.invocation: (aside) lol that's the second time it's tried that approach
examples.expected_output: Message visible to humans; ignored by Devin
examples.scenario: Human-only thread chatter without disturbing Devin's run

purpose: Put Devin to sleep on the current task. Send any message in the thread to wake Devin back up.

examples.invocation: sleep
examples.expected_output: Devin enters sleep state; will resume on next message
examples.scenario: Pausing while waiting on external dependency (CI, third-party review)

purpose: Put Devin to sleep AND archive the session. Cleaner than `sleep` for sessions you're done with.

examples.invocation: archive
examples.expected_output: Session archived; thread deactivated
examples.scenario: Wrapping up a completed Devin run

purpose: End the current Devin session immediately.

examples.invocation: EXIT
examples.expected_output: Session ends; thread deactivated
examples.scenario: Aborting a session that's gone off-track

purpose: Show the available inline keywords and functions. Available in Microsoft Teams.

examples.invocation: help
examples.expected_output: List of !ask, !deep, mute, unmute, sleep, archive, EXIT, etc.
examples.scenario: Teaching new users the keyword set

purpose: Slack-only: launch a Dana session (Cognition's data-analyst agent variant). Equivalent to `!dana` triggers in the Slack inline-keyword set.

examples.invocation: !dana what was the p99 latency for the checkout service in the last 7 days?
examples.expected_output: Dana queries telemetry and posts the answer
examples.scenario: Quick analytics question in Slack

purpose: Slack-only: invoke a named playbook macro at session start. Examples include user-defined `![ship-it]`, `![investigate]`, etc.

flags.name: [macro_name]
flags.doc: Macro name from the customer's playbook configuration.

flags.name: <message>
flags.doc: Optional task instructions appended to the playbook context.

examples.invocation: ![ship-it] PR 4567
examples.expected_output: Devin starts a session using the 'ship-it' playbook on PR 4567
examples.scenario: Playbook-driven Slack-triggered run

purpose: Slack-only: launch a fast-mode Devin session. Trades off depth for speed.

examples.invocation: !fast fix the typo in README.md line 47
examples.expected_output: Devin runs in fast mode and opens a one-line PR quickly
examples.scenario: Trivial change in Slack

purpose: Trigger a Devin session from Jira by assigning the ticket to Devin's service account. Uses the default playbook configured in the Jira integration settings.

examples.invocation: Set Assignee to Devin on JIRA-1234
examples.expected_output: Devin opens a session against the ticket using the default playbook
examples.scenario: Standard ticket-driven Devin trigger

purpose: Trigger Devin with a specific playbook by adding a label whose name matches the macro (e.g., `!plan`, `!implement`, `!triage`).

flags.name: label
flags.doc: Playbook macro label name. Must already exist in the Jira project.

examples.invocation: Add label `!plan` to JIRA-5678
examples.expected_output: Devin starts a session using the !plan playbook
examples.scenario: Plan-only run on a new feature ticket

command: [Jira] Add `devin` label (or any label containing 'devin' as a standalone word)
purpose: Trigger Devin using the default playbook by adding a generic devin-label. Word-boundary matching, case-insensitive: `devin`, `Devin`, `devin-workshop`, `devin-task` all match. `devinworkshop` and `devin_workshop` do NOT.

examples.invocation: Add label `devin` to JIRA-9012
examples.expected_output: Devin starts a session using the default playbook
examples.scenario: Quickest manual trigger

purpose: Trigger Devin from a Jira ticket comment. Devin uses the comment text as the task instruction (no playbook applied). If a session already exists for the ticket, the comment is forwarded to that session.

examples.invocation: Comment on JIRA-1234: '@Devin please reproduce the failure described in the issue and propose a fix'
examples.expected_output: Devin opens a session and starts working
examples.scenario: Ad-hoc instructions on a non-default ticket

purpose: Trigger Devin from Linear via assignment. Uses the default playbook (`!plan` for new connections).

examples.invocation: Assign LIN-456 to Devin
examples.expected_output: Devin opens a session via Linear's agent-session UI
examples.scenario: Standard Linear-driven trigger

purpose: Trigger Devin with a specific playbook by adding a label from the 'Devin Playbooks' label group.

flags.name: label
flags.doc: Playbook label synced from Devin's integration settings.

examples.invocation: Add label `!implement` to LIN-789
examples.expected_output: Devin starts a session using the !implement playbook
examples.scenario: Implementation run on a planned ticket

purpose: Trigger Devin from a Linear ticket comment with custom instructions. No playbook applied.

examples.invocation: Comment on LIN-101: '@Devin investigate the reported memory leak in the worker pool'
examples.expected_output: Devin opens a session and begins investigation
examples.scenario: Ad-hoc task on a Linear ticket

command: [GitHub] github.com/settings/installations > Devin.ai Integration > Configure > Danger zone > Uninstall
purpose: Remove Devin's GitHub App installation from a GitHub organization — required when migrating an org's Devin integration to a different Devin account.

examples.invocation: github.com/settings/installations > Devin.ai > Configure > scroll to Danger zone > Uninstall
examples.expected_output: Devin's app uninstalled from GitHub side
examples.scenario: Migrating from a stale Devin org/enterprise

command: [Slack] Workspace Admin > Configure apps > Installed Apps > Devin > App Details > Configuration tab > Bot User > rename
purpose: Rename Devin in a Slack workspace (the bot's display name).

examples.invocation: Slack admin > Configure apps > Devin > App Details > Configuration > Bot User > 'Robobot'
examples.expected_output: Bot now appears as @Robobot in the workspace
examples.scenario: Workspace branding

command: [Devin run UI] menu > Enable Slack notifications
purpose: Enable per-run private Slack notifications. Devin DMs the user on status updates for that session.

examples.invocation: Open a run, click menu > Enable Slack notifications
examples.expected_output: DMs from Devin on every status update for that run
examples.scenario: Async monitoring of a long-running session

command: [AWS] Create Network Load Balancer with security groups for Devin egress IPs
purpose: Stand up an NLB to front a self-hosted SCM/artifact endpoint, configured with security-group rules per Devin egress IP. Required for the manual-security-groups self-hosted setup pattern (NLB preserves source IPs).

flags.name: security-groups
flags.doc: Security group with rules for each Devin egress IP.

flags.name: target-group
flags.doc: Target group pointing at the internal service.

examples.invocation: Create NLB; attach SG with 7 inbound TCP/443 rules (one per Devin egress IP); attach target group pointing at GitLab self-hosted
examples.expected_output: Public NLB endpoint reachable only from Devin's IPs
examples.scenario: Self-hosted GitLab exposure to Devin

command: [AWS] Create Application Load Balancer + WAF with IP-allowlist rule
purpose: Stand up an ALB fronting a self-hosted endpoint, with AWS WAF enforcing IP allowlist. Recommended for most use cases. NOTE: ALB NATs source IPs — for artifact repos, IP allowlisting must ALSO be configured at the artifact repo itself.

flags.name: waf-acl
flags.doc: WAF ACL with an IP-set rule listing Devin egress IPs.

examples.invocation: Create ALB; attach WAF ACL with IP-allowlist rule referencing Devin's 7 egress IPs
examples.expected_output: ALB rejects traffic outside Devin's IPs at WAF level
examples.scenario: Self-hosted GitLab + Artifactory behind one ALB

purpose: Publish a DNS record pointing at the load balancer that fronts the self-hosted endpoint, so Devin can reach it via a stable domain name.

flags.name: --change-batch
flags.doc: JSON change batch describing the new A/AAAA record.

examples.invocation: aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch file://dns-change.json
examples.expected_output: DNS record propagates; Devin can connect via gitlab.yourcompany.com
examples.scenario: Final step of self-hosted SCM onboarding

command: Email enterprise@cognition.ai with self-hosted SCM URL + artifact repo URL + auth requirements
purpose: Hand off self-hosted-SCM/artifacts integration to Cognition support after the network plumbing is ready. Cognition completes the connection from their side.

examples.invocation: Email enterprise@cognition.ai: 'Self-hosted GitLab at https://gitlab.acme.com (NLB-fronted, 7 Devin IPs allowed); Artifactory at https://artifacts.acme.com; service account `devin-bot`'
examples.expected_output: Cognition completes the integration setup on their side
examples.scenario: Final hand-off in self-hosted SCM onboarding
